Subject: IAC assembly request: TF/Helm/Ansible composition + network-policy shims

Hi Dev,

Thanks again for taking this on. Attached is an initial diff (iac-assembly.patch) that our infra team put together for the private deployment in our VPC. High level: we want a small composition that stitches Terraform (VPC, subnets, NAT gateways), Helm charts (service manifests + network-policy-shims chart), and a handful of Ansible roles for host-level tunables.

Two asks from Acme side:
- Can Redwood review the proposed module boundaries and recommend changes to ensure we can meet your recommended gating for private deploys (iam, audit logs, egress controls)?
- We need a short list of CI gating items (tfsec/conftest rules, helm value pinning, artifact signing) that must pass before we promote to staging.

Notes:
- We prefer a thin network-policy "shim" chart that can be applied per-environment (dev/staging/prod) to lock down pod-to-pod flows.
- We need evidence for compliance: policy matrix mapping (who requested which allowlist) and a plan for egress NAT logging.

Could you and your team review and reply with an initial take by EOD (PST) tomorrow? If it's easier, we can schedule a 30-min sync — happy to host.

Attachments: iac-assembly.patch (diff - Terraform/Helm/Ansible snippets)

Thanks,
Bethany Owens
Head of Cloud Operations
Acme Analytics

Bethany —

Appreciate the diff. Quick read-through notes below (initial, high-level). I cc'd Neha and Kimberly for the security/CI specifics — they should add concrete gating rules.

Initial take (tl;dr: split responsibilities, keep network-policy shims minimal, require pipeline policy checks):
- Module boundaries: separate concerns — terraform/network, terraform/iam, helm/apps, helm/network-policy-shims, ansible/host-config. Avoid cross-cutting templates inside a single repo; compose via a small orchestration repo referencing the modules.
- Network-policy-shims: keep it as a Helm umbrella chart with environment overlays (values files per env). The chart should generate Kubernetes NetworkPolicy CRs only — no service manifests. This makes rollbacks safer.
- Terraform: state separation per environment (remote backend + workspace per env). Keep NAT and egress rules in a clearly named module (vpc-egress) to make audit easier.
- CI gating (short list): tfsec on plan, terraform fmt/validate, helm lint + policy (conftest/OPA), signed chart artifacts for prod, and an image digest pinning policy.
- Evidence: network-policy-matrix.xlsx will help map owners -> justifications. We'll want that attached to PRs that change allowlists.

Open questions for your team:
1) Do you expect any cross-VPC peering to other Acme accounts? That changes the egress model.
2) Are you using an internal registry that supports image signing?

Proposed next step: Neha and Kimberly will reply with an explicit checklist and example CI snippets. If you can share a quick call slot tomorrow 10–12 PST, I can join.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Dev / Bethany —

Adding a security checklist and some concrete gating rules. I attached a flattened matrix (network-policy-matrix.xlsx) with columns: service, source, dest, port/proto, justification, owner, evidence-link. Please ensure every allowlist entry in the shim chart references the owner and evidence link (PR or confluence page).

Security gating (must-have for staging->prod):
- Terraform: terraform fmt + validate, terraform plan scanned by tfsec (block severity HIGH), policy-as-code checks with conftest for required tags and encryption-at-rest. Remote state must be encrypted and access-limited to the CI service account.
- Helm: helm lint + chart schema validation; conftest/OPA rule that disallows hostNetwork, privileged containers, and requires networkPolicy: enforced. Charts for prod must be signed and checksummed in pipeline.
- Kubernetes network policies: every generated NetworkPolicy must include a comment (annotation) referencing the matrix entry id and an owner. No wide allowlists (0.0.0.0/0) except where justified and approved.
- Ansible: roles must validate variables with schema checks; secrets must not be embedded — use Vault/KMS references only.
- Observability: egress NAT logs forwarded to central logging for 90 days (we require 90d for Acme compliance). Kubernetes audit logs retained per your retention policy and accessible for at least 180 days.
- Tests: add a small integration test in CI that deploys to an ephemeral namespace, runs k8s-network-policy-test-suite to assert deny-by-default semantics, and performs a connectivity matrix. Failure = block.

Quick implementation notes:
- I suggest adding an automated PR labeler that requires a "security-evidence" checklist before merge.
- For conftest rules, I can drop a starter bundle (rego) in a repo we share.

Attachments: network-policy-matrix.xlsx

If you want, we can gate on a single boolean in the release pipeline once all evidence links are present. That is simpler for Acme operators.

– Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — fwding a concise CI/CD playbook outline so Acme can slot into their pipelines. High-level items we will require for a Redwood private deployment acceptance: 

CI/CD playbook (outline):
1) Pull-request stage (authors):
   - terraform fmt/validate, helm lint, ansible-lint run locally and in CI
   - tfsec scan on terraform plan. tfsec failures of severity >= HIGH must block.
   - conftest/OPA (rego) rules executed on all charts and k8s manifests.
2) Merge gate (staging deploy):
   - Terraform apply to staging with remote state and a sandboxed service account
   - Helm chart artifact build -> sign -> push to registry (signed artifacts required for prod)
   - Run network-policy-test-suite (ephemeral namespace) that validates the matrix from network-policy-matrix.xlsx
3) Release gate (prod promote):
   - Artifact digest pin required; no floating tags
   - Release job verifies evidence links present for every change that touches network policy or egress
   - Automated rollback hook: if health checks degrade >5% in 10 minutes, rollback to previous chart revision automatically.
4) Post-release compliance:
   - Export audit logs + NAT flow logs to bucket with 90d retention; generate weekly report for Acme SOC.

Implementation specifics and examples I can commit to a shared repo:
- Jenkins/GitHub Actions example for tfsec + conftest (I will add a sample workflow).
- Helm umbrella chart pattern for network-policy-shims plus values-per-env.
- Ansible role parameter schema using ansible-lint and molecule tests.

Next steps: Dev/Neha — I'll push the sample workflows and a minimal repo structure (terraform/, charts/network-policy-shims/, ansible/roles/) to the Drive link and PR template that requires the "security-evidence" checklist. Bethany — can you confirm whether Acme wants the signed charts in your registry or a Redwood-managed proxy? If you want us to host signing metadata we can support that as an option.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Platform Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
